Apple is rolling out the first developer and public beta (RC) builds of macOS 26.6 in preparation for the official release. Here’s what’s new in this update.

macOS 26.6 Candidate Release 1 starts rolling out

Following five developer and public beta builds, Apple has officially released the first release candidate (RC) of macOS 26.6, paving the way for a final update that could launch as early as next week.

Readers familiar with the beta cycle will know that macOS 26.6 is light on new features, focusing instead on bug fixes and system refinements.

However, for users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, this release may pack an important feature.

The release notes for iOS 26.6 RC state that the system “refines Spotlight indexing in preparation for iOS 27,” so macOS 26.6 should include the same change. We’ll update this report once Apple publishes the full release notes for macOS 26.6 RC.

Another change Apple specifically highlighted in the first beta was a fix for an issue where certain apps were misidentified as Intel-only and triggered macOS deprecation alerts. Apple later noted that bugs related to the ecosystem and HealthKit had also been resolved, but didn’t reveal much else about this update.

That said, we’ll dig into this release closely and report back to you with anything noteworthy. The macOS 26.6 RC build number is 25G70.

How to install macOS 26.6 RC

Below are the steps to install macOS Tahoe 26.6 RC:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open “System Settings”
  • Navigate to “General” → “Software Update”
  • Tap the “i” icon next to “Beta Updates”
  • From the drop-down menu in the top-right corner, select “macOS Developer Tahoe Beta”
  • Tap “Done”
